name: Reactive Power Exposure
trigger_conditions: motors, compressors, chillers, pumps, conveyors or chargers plausible
physical_basis: Inductive and nonlinear loads can create reactive power or power-quality exposure even when total annual kWh appears ordinary.
operational_basis: Load sequencing, compensation absence and equipment mix can shape utility penalties and hidden capacity pressure.
financial_mechanism: PF penalties, kvar charges or demand interactions can create a cost story invisible to aggregate EUI analysis.
typical_false_assumption: Aggregate consumption is enough to understand cost and capacity pressure.
hypothesis: Reactive power or power-quality exposure may be material if inductive or nonlinear loads exist and compensation is absent or unknown.
rival_hypotheses: demand structure dominates without PF or reactive exposure
inductive load is too small to matter
evidence_required: utility bills showing kW, kWh, kvar, PF or demand structure
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: utility evidence shows PF or reactive penalties
falsification_conditions: no PF penalties or reactive charges
allowed_claim_language: Power-quality exposure is a plausible hypothesis requiring tariff and utility-bill validation.
prohibited_claim_language: The facility has reactive power losses.
financial_exposure_if_true: hidden demand or PF penalty exposure
capacity and tariff pressure misread as generic inefficiency
financial_exposure_if_false: attention should shift to other rival hypotheses
stop_conditions: utility and tariff evidence bound PF relevance
escalation_conditions: power-quality study requested only if bills and tariff remain ambiguous
example_outputs: If power factor is unmanaged, part of the cost and capacity problem may be invisible to standard EUI analysis.
tests: manufacturing and utility-heavy cases should activate this when inductive load and tariff remain unresolved
